nodes.summary: For every bit $c$, every natural number $r \le 255$ and every finite bit list $w$, every entry of the compression $C(c, r, w)$ of $w$ from the pending run $(c, r)$ is at most $255$.
nodes.title: Compression from a short pending run emits counts at most 255

nodes.summary: For a bit $c$, a natural number $r$ and a finite bit list $w$, the compression $C(c, r, w)$ of $w$ from the pending run $(c, r)$ is the list of natural numbers defined by recursion on $w$. If $w$ is empty, $C(c, r, w)$ is the one-entry list $(r)$. If $w$ is a bit $b$ followed by a list $w'$, then $C(c, r, w)$ is $r$ followed by $C(\lnot c, 1, w')$ when $b \ne c$; it is $255$, then $0$, followed by $C(c, 1, w')$…
nodes.title: Run-length compression from a pending run

nodes.summary: For every finite bit list $w$, every entry of the run-length compression of $w$ is at most $255$.
nodes.title: Run lengths fit in 8 bits

nodes.summary: The run-length compression of a finite bit list $w$ is $C(0, 0, w)$, the compression of $w$ from an empty pending run of zero bits. It lists the lengths of the maximal runs of $w$, alternating between zeros and ones and starting with a possibly empty run of zeros; a run of length $n > 255$ is written as $255, 0, 255, 0, \dots, 255, 0, m$ with $1 \le m \le 255$.
nodes.title: Run-length compression

nodes.summary: For every finite bit list $w$, the run-length expansion of the run-length compression of $w$ is $w$.
nodes.title: Run-length expansion inverts compression

nodes.summary: For every bit $c$, every natural number $r$ and every finite bit list $w$, the expansion from the starting bit $c$ of the compression $C(c, r, w)$ is the list of $r$ copies of $c$ followed by $w$.
nodes.title: Expansion recovers the pending run and the input

nodes.summary: For every bit $c$ and every list $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers, the expansion $E(c, (n_1, \dots, n_k))$ has length $n_1 + \dots + n_k$.
nodes.title: Length of an expansion from a starting bit

nodes.summary: For a bit $c$ and a list $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers, the expansion $E(c, (n_1, \dots, n_k))$ is the bit list obtained by concatenating, for $i = 1, \dots, k$ in order, $n_i$ copies of $c$ when $i$ is odd and $n_i$ copies of $\lnot c$ when $i$ is even.
nodes.title: Run-length expansion from a starting bit

nodes.summary: For every list $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers, the run-length expansion of $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ has length $n_1 + \dots + n_k$.
nodes.title: Length of a run-length expansion

nodes.summary: The run-length expansion of a list $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers is $E(0, (n_1, \dots, n_k))$, the expansion from the zero bit: the bit list obtained by concatenating, for $i = 1, \dots, k$ in order, $n_i$ zeros when $i$ is odd and $n_i$ ones when $i$ is even.
nodes.title: Run-length expansion

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
